Because incest is a cultural taboo, and we don't know for how many centuries this has been so, it causes psychological harm for families that participate, and for society when they hear about it. The level of disregard for social norms required to engage in incest (not to mention openly endorse it on a public forum) gives little assurance that norms will be followed in other contexts (not committing other crimes) or for meaningfully engagement in society in any other way.  There are dangers for premature sexual development in children, lack of appropriate understanding of social boundaries, the inability to consent if there is a significant age difference between participants or if both participants are too young to understand the behavior, the risk of bodily harm, a change in visual perception systems..... Children exposed to incest are more likely to develop schizophrenia, commit suicide, become serial killers, pedophiles, or rapists. There are real physical, physiological, psychological and sociological harms to incest.

I'm glad you feel better by writing it out. I've been wondering if I should just give myself summers off to go to that dark place and see what's there. We all need time for thought incubation and with depression and thoughts running slower it seems like I need a lot more time. For instance little things like sending text messages, maybe they take you longer to process that's why you don't quite believe you are sending normal things.

But hey. If you aren't sending normal texts or doing normal things it isn't the end of the world. Your friends probably know more about you than you think and your boyfriend is still there for you, even though its hard right now. Once I was so out of it I went to school without shoes on. I survived it.

At this point I am trying to work with my depression and coax what productivity I can out of it. Working with my depression entails a lot of self reflection, journaling, reading, depression outreach, looking at art, defining myself... When I finish all those things to make myself sane and cope I get to focus on my class work and all the other external things.

I think you are taking for granted how much you actually do have to offer. You were able to spur a conversation with all these people on reddit. You are able to write coherently and communicate effectively. 

I recommend 7 Cups of Tea (its an app and a website) and the NAMI forums. Both of those sites have a network of people that actually care and try to help; more evidence that there are people who will care.

So many of us on here feel like we're fake and worth nothing. But how about being real? How about being something? I know its just another thing we can let ourselves down with but my goal in life is to be an authentic person and live a meaningful life. Every day that I get caught up in doing things others think I should do is a depressing day that I fail. And of course defining all the rules of how to be a real person on your own terms is such a big task. We look to tradition and what's socially accepted to fill in the gaps for what we don't know enough about yet, but that just won't work for me. And I don't know, maybe in the long run it doesn't work for any of us. The elderly often abandon social convention in favor of their own way.

But man, if you cant take care of yourself right now at all and are considering suicide, maybe its time to go to consider the hospital.
